concepts.question: Is any part of either lung field whiter than the surrounding dark, air-filled lung?

absent.text: both lung fields read uniformly dark from apex to base apart from ribs, vessels and the heart shadow

subtle.text: a faintly paler zone hard to separate from overlying rib or vessel shadow

definite.text: an area plainly whiter than the matching region of the opposite lung, with a discernible edge

concepts.question: How much of the combined lung area is taken up by whiter, less dark regions?

none.text: no zone is whiter than the surrounding lung; whiteness is confined to ribs, heart and hilar vessels

small_patch.text: patchy whiteness too small to fill a lobe, below the magnitude WHO requires for primary-endpoint consolidation

lobe_sized.text: a dense or fluffy opacity occupying a portion or the whole of one lobe

most_of_both_lungs.text: whiteness covering an entire lung, or spread through the greater part of both lung fields

concepts.question: Where the lung looks whiter, are the fine vessel lines still visible through it, or completely hidden by solid whiteness?

none.text: vessel and airway margins stay as crisp as those in the opposite lung throughout

hazy_lines_visible.text: a veil of added whiteness through which vessel and airway margins can still be traced

solid_lines_hidden.text: homogeneous whiteness that hides vessel margins and airway walls, dense or fluffy rather than lacy

concepts.question: Are fine linear, streaky or net-like white lines spread through both lung fields?

absent.text: only smoothly tapering vessel branches; no extra streaky or net-like white lines

mild.text: a few extra streaky lines beyond the tapering vessels, limited to one lung or to a couple of zones

marked.text: linear and patchy densities in a lacy net-like pattern involving both lungs

concepts.question: Inside a whiter region, are branching dark tube-like lines visible against the white?

absent.text: no dark branching tubes stand out within any whiter region of lung

present.text: one or more dark air-filled bronchi traced against surrounding white airless lung

concepts.question: Around the central root of each lung, do the branching markings look thickened, cuffed or ring-shaped rather than fine and tapering?

absent.text: bronchial walls beside the hilar vessels are hairline thin and end-on bronchi show no ring

mild.text: a few hilar branches carry a visible cuff or ring wall, the rest still fine and tapering

marked.text: coarse cuffed walls and ring shadows on most branches radiating from both hila

concepts.question: Is the outline of the lower heart edge, or of either dome of the diaphragm, blurred or lost where lung meets it?

absent.text: the lower heart edge and both diaphragm domes are traced as sharp unbroken lines

partial.text: part of the lower cardiac edge or of one diaphragm dome is blurred while the rest stays traceable

complete.text: the lower cardiac edge or a whole diaphragm dome is not depicted where opaque lung abuts it

concepts.question: Is either lower outer angle between the diaphragm and the chest wall filled in or rounded rather than a sharp point?

absent.text: both outer angles between diaphragm and chest wall taper to a sharp point

mild.text: one angle is rounded or shallowly filled so that its apex is no longer a point

marked.text: fluid fills the angle and tracks up the lateral chest wall well above the diaphragm
